chunks: When Saul led the armies, he said: 'God will test you with a river; whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except the one who scoops a handful with his hand.' So they drank from it, except a few of them. When he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said: 'We have no strength today against Goliath and his forces.' Those who believed they would meet God said: 'How many a small band has defeated a large band by the permission of God. And God is with the patient.'
ai.seo_question: What was the test of the river given to Saul's army and what does it signify about patience and divine permission?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this trial (ibtila') of drinking from the river is often interpreted as a test of self-restraint and obedience rather than mere thirst, highlighting the transition from a large, undisciplined force to a core of faithful believers. The subsequent confidence of the 'few' against Goliath's 'many' underscores the principle that divine victory (nasr) relies on spiritual steadfastness (sabr) and God's permission (bi-idhnillah), a theme frequently cited in discussions of Imam Ali's smaller forces at battles like Khaybar or Siffin.
